RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

The panel's composition is weak evidence on its own — it's a common artefact of who sits on school boards, and all-male panels appoint women routinely. Raise it as context, never as your main argument.

Your strong point is the qualifications comparison: a master's in educational leadership and five years actually doing the deputy's job against "courses" and classroom years. If the formal criteria ranked leadership training and management experience, the appointment needs explaining.

Press hard on the unanswered request instead. In most jurisdictions you're entitled to written reasons, and if the less-qualified candidate's selection stays unexplained, the burden can shift to the employer. Send a dated follow-up, cite the relevant equality body, and keep everything in writing.
